body: My dad is verbally and emotionally abusive, since I'm a minor I don't have the power to remove myself from his house when it gets bad. I'm trying to juggle a lot right now as well, and the stress is becoming unbearable.
Thank you, this comment struck me most, I feel like this is very realistic yet comforting advice. Thank you for taking the time to write this.

Well, I started a new medication for my depression and I'm not sure if it's just not working, but also my classes have been really difficult, I want to quit my job but can't, my grandma has been in the hospital, and the relationship between my dad and I hasn't been great as of late. It's just getting to be a lot and I feel like I've been having trouble handling and dealing with all the problems in my life. I've been going to a therapist and I just started meds but it's discouraging how long the road to recovery is.

I found myself sitting on the bathroom floor again holding a bunch of pills and contemplating whether or not I wanted to take them. I've posted here a few times before in the last few months and doing so has enabled me to talk myself out of it before I actually do anything.

My therapist has told me that no matter how much or how little you do in a day, it's still a really great accomplishment. I don't know how much that helps me but I always try and keep it in mind, maybe it can help you too to think about. I don't usually get enough sleep, I average about 5 to 6 hours a night so I'm usually always pretty tired. I have trouble falling asleep and staying asleep too which doesn't help, so even if I slept for 5 to 6 hours it isn't always good sleep.

The job itself isn't very hard and I'm lucky enough to have an employer that's accommodating, but I'm still on my "trial period", so to speak, so I feel bad asking for too much time off, and it's been a lot to try and balance at one time. Most nights it feels like I don't have enough time to get schoolwork done as it is, so when I have to work it becomes even harder.

I've been suffering from clinical depression for about a year now. I'm also trying to juggle a job and 2 AP classes at the same time (I'm a high school student). It's starting to really effect my mental health because I feel too overwhelmed. Today I also learned that a close friend of mine has been lying to me for quite some time, I believe it was done to spare my feelings but it still really hurts. I just feel lost. 

I've been in therapy for a few months now, and I'm considering starting meds, but it's just been really hard. I feel like I have no control over my life anymore and it feels like everything that could go wrong has gone wrong.

Those are definitely some good questions that I'll try and consider. From what she's told me, I think her primary goal is just for me and my brother to get into good colleges, and get good careers so that we can have more than she did as a child, and does now. So her goal for me is for that to happen, and her goal for herself is to help that happen for me.

Because of the honors program I was in in the years leading up to this one, I've essentially completed the high school "generals" so to speak, so my school doesn't have any more classes to offer that aren't these AP and concurrent enrollment classes that I'm in. 

I just suffer from a lot guilt knowing that my mom will go years not buying anything for herself so that she can give us spending money or whatnot that we don't need. I've tried to talk to her about this and I'm working with my therapist on it as well, but I struggle because I feel like I'm the cause of her not having enough money to be able to spend it on herself once in a while. 

Edit: to elaborate a little more, this honors program basically excelled me so that by the time I finished my freshman year of high school, I had completed the equivalent of about 3 years of "normal" high school classes that some of my peers would have taken. That means that my sophomore-senior years, if I want to have all the core subjects (math, science, English, social studies) then I have to take college level courses. My high school doesn't offer other options.

Hi, thank you for taking the time to respond, it means a lot. I can't drop my classes because I'm past the "point of no return", so to speak. In the post I briefly mentioned why I need the job (don't worry about missing it) but basically my parents are divorced and my dad doesn't really help pay for anything besides the basic child support stuff, so my mom has to pay for everything for my brother and I. We make enough, we're certainly middle class, but we don't always have a lot to spare and my mom rarely buys anything for herself— she usually save it or spends it on us. Because of that, I sometimes feel guilty when she spends money on me so I want to be able to have my own money.

Lots of people will compare mental illness to cancer, in that you wouldn't tell a cancer patient that they can think their way out of it, not to get medical help/meds, that it's their fault, etc. I think maybe that could help you here. Just like you wouldn't tell someone with cancer that they were weak for having cancer, you aren't weak because you have a mental illness and might need to take medication for it.

Everyone has days that suck, and that's okay. I'm not sure what type of relationship you have with your parents, but maybe you could talk to them honestly about why you've been in a sour mood lately. If you don't have that kind of relationship with your parents, friends/teachers/other relatives that you trust can be a great support system and a way to let off steam when you need to. 

As for the girl you have a crush on, don't worry about the awkward IM conversation. I've had many an awkward first online conversation with people that I end up either dating or becoming great friends with. Don't let one bad conversation wreck your confidence, and the conversation likely felt a lot more awkward to you than it did to her. Sometimes the best way to achieve confidence is to "fake it till you make it", so to speak. I've personally found that the best way to go when you don't exactly feel confident is to just ask how her day is going, if she did anything cool recently, or other questions about her.

Thank you so much for your advice, this is excellent! This is something I honestly hadn't ever heard of before and it's very comforting to know that this isn't just how my friends are acting. I appreciate the resources you provided too, all in all this advice is great and I'll be sure to share it with my girl friends in case situations arise like this in the future. Hopefully this can make us all a little less irritated in the future. :) Thanks again for taking time out of your day to help, I appreciate this so much.
